source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Clearly describe the appliance name and model, along with its serial number.
3. Document the date and time of the safety check.
4. Record the specific standards or regulations the appliance is being tested against.
5. Detail the test method(s) used for the inspection.
6. Clearly outline all observed defects or faults during the safety check.
   - Visual inspection issues (e.g., frayed cords, burned marks, broken parts)
   - Functional issues (e.g., overheating, sparks, intermittent operation)
7. Note any tests that the appliance failed to pass according to the specific criteria.
8. Record meter readings or for digital testers, attach a screenshot of the results.
9. Include comments regarding the severity of the failure and any immediate risks or hazards.
10. State whether the appliance is safe for immediate use, requires repair before use, or is unsafe and must be decommissioned.
11. Signature of the person who conducted the inspection.
